openFindings.path: __tests__/domain/v3-06-repair-sync-authorization.test.ts (Finding #1 failure-injection test, lines 972-978 and assertion at 1013)
openFindings.problem: The rewritten failure-injection test injects a failing repo built as {...originalContributions, seed: throw, create: throw}. originalContributions is a SyncRecordingContributionRepository class instance; spreading a class instance copies only own enumerable fields (inner, syncState) and loses all prototype methods (getById, getByHousehold, ...). The production MaterializingSyncState.applyDeltas -> materializeDeltas -> upsertWithConflictResolution calls repos.contributions.getById(record.id) BEFORE seed, so the actual error is 'repos.contributions.getById is not a function' instead of the intended 'Simulated materialization failure'. The assertion expect(caughtError.message).toContain('Simulated materialization failure') fails, so the test does not prove the intended scenario (a repo error during materialization rolling back cursor + all business tables).
openFindings.evidence: Independent npx jest: 'repo error during materialization does NOT advance cursor and does NOT partially update ANY business table' fails — 'Expected substring: Simulated materialization failure / Received string: repos.contributions.getById is not a function'. SyncMaterializer.ts line 213 calls repos.contributions.getById(record.id) before seed at line 219.
openFindings.requiredFix: Inject the failing repo while preserving the prototype chain, e.g. const failing = Object.create(originalContributions); failing.seed = () => { throw new Error('Simulated materialization failure'); }; failing.create = async () => { throw new Error('Simulated materialization failure'); }; (or a Proxy), then assign (repos as any).contributions = failing before pullDeltas and restore afterwards. Keep the assertions that the cursor did not advance and every business table is unchanged.
openFindings.verification: The test passes with the intended 'Simulated materialization failure' error and still asserts cursor <= 1 and all 7 business tables unchanged after rollback.

openFindings.path: __tests__/infrastructure/repositories.test.ts (V3-06 REPAIR Finding #5 describe block, lines 1013-1105; pull call at line 1064, assertion at line 1075)
openFindings.problem: The new SQLite factory-wiring test does not wire the repos 'exactly as the factory does'. It constructs raw SQLite repos + SyncRecording wrappers but passes the raw SqliteSyncStateRepository (baseSyncState) directly to pullDeltas instead of wrapping it in a MaterializingSyncState as the factory does (RepositoryFactory.ts lines 441-442: materializingSync = new MaterializingSyncState(baseSyncState, () => repos)). The raw SqliteSyncStateRepository.applyDeltas is buffer-only (SqliteRepositories.ts lines 1168-1201: writes sync_records, never materializes into business tables), so the remote delta never becomes a readable business record and the assertion expect(entry).not.toBeNull() fails.
openFindings.evidence: Independent npx jest: 'factory-wired SQLite repos: remote delta materializes into business table' fails at line 1075 (entry is null). Test line 1064: 'await pull(baseSyncState, HH, ...)' — baseSyncState is a raw SqliteSyncStateRepository, not a MaterializingSyncState. The objective explicitly requires 'raw SQLite repos + SyncRecording* wrappers + MaterializingSyncState' or an exported testable factory path.
openFindings.requiredFix: Wrap baseSyncState in a MaterializingSyncState (export the class from RepositoryFactory or replicate the factory wiring in the test) and pass that wrapped sync state to pullDeltas, so applyDeltas materializes the remote delta into the business table. Keep the assertions: remote delta -> business record readable; local write via wrapped repo -> getDirtyRecords returns the payload; pushDeltas sends it.
openFindings.verification: The test passes with entry.label === 'Remote via factory' and entry.value === 30, and the local-write/push assertions still hold.
